newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay bourse shifts 28 stocks to 'A' group.
newsitem.headline: Bombay bourse shifts 28 stocks to 'A' group.

text.p: The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) said on Friday it would shift 28 stocks to its more active A group shares from the B1 group in a move designed to improve liquidity in the market.
The changes will take effect from October 28, BSE said in a statement.

The stocks which will be shifted to the A group include Andhra Valley Power Supply Co, Apollo Tyres, Ballarpur Industries, Bharat Heavy Electricals, Bharat Petroleum Corporation, Britannia Industries, Cadbury India, Castrol India, Century Textiles, Dr Reddy's Laboratories, Escorts, Hindustan Motors, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation, Industrial Development Bank of India, Industrial Finance Corporation of India, Indian Rayon, ITC Bharachalam, Mastergain, Nestle India, Oriental Bank of Commerce, Ranbaxy Laboratories, Raymond, Steel Authority of India, SCICI, Siemens, Sterlite Industries, Thermax and United Phosphorus.
"With this addition the number of scrips in A group will go upto 60. It is hoped that this move will improve liquidity in the market," BSE said.
